# Encyclopaedia Mundi

> A knowledge research and discovery site. Ask a question in your own words and
> get a direct answer built from Wikipedia and Wikidata, with the source behind
> every claim. Static, no build step, no account, no tracking.

Canonical origin: https://encyclopaediamundi.pages.dev

## What the site does

- Search: a question becomes a search over Wikipedia in twelve languages.
- Answer: the best-matching article is rebuilt around the question — a lead,
  the sentences that answer it, numbered topics, and the source.
- Chat (Amigo): the same sources handed to a language model with one rule —
  answer only from them, cite them, and say so when they do not contain the
  answer. When no article matches, the question is answered as conversation
  and labelled "General answer" instead of being given a false citation.
- Library: one search across Wikipedia, Wikiquote and Wikisource.
- On this day: events, births and deaths for any date.

## Pages

- /                       the app (ask, explore, today, library, sources, saved)
- /chat/                  Amigo, the conversational surface
- /articles/              thirteen complete articles
- /topics/                every subject written here
- /questions/             the questions the site is built to answer
- /research/              the research desk
- /how-it-works/          ask, research, filter, explain, cite
- /help/                  what the badges mean and what is stored
- /sitemap.xml            every crawlable URL

## Rules the answers follow

1. A factual sentence that came from an article is shown with that article.
2. A model is never allowed to fill a gap from memory in a source-backed answer.
3. A citation that points at nothing is removed before the answer is shown.
4. A general answer is labelled as one, and carries no citations.
